REVISE
<<<END VERDICT>>>
<<<FINDINGS>>>
- [BLOCKER] loop.py: `failed_gates = sorted({r["stage"] for r in result["rounds"] if not r.get("ok", True)})` — This assumes every failed round has a `stage` key whose value is the gate name. If any round dict lacks `stage` (e.g. a round that failed before a stage was assigned, or a round whose `stage` is `None`), the set will contain `None`/missing values, and the ledger will record `"gate": None` or `"gate": [None, "static"]`. In `report.py`, `gate is None` is treated as "unmeasurable legacy," so a genuinely-failed ticket with a `None` stage will be silently excluded from the distribution — the exact class of bug this ticket is about. The code never validates that `r["stage"]` exists or is a real gate name.

- [BLOCKER] loop.py: `failed_gates = sorted({r["stage"] for r in result["rounds"] if not r.get("ok", True)})` — When a ticket is rejected at the protected-paths gate (the early-return path at line ~452), `result["rounds"]` is empty. That path now hardcodes `"gate": "protected"`, which is correct. But any *other* early-return or exception path that writes a ledger entry (or any path where `result["rounds"]` is empty for a non-protected rejection) will produce `failed_gates = []`, so no `gate` field is written. That ticket will then appear as "unmeasurable legacy" in the report even though it was rejected by a real gate. The fix only covers two of the ledger write sites; any third site is silently broken.

- [MAJOR] loop.py: `ledger_record["gate"] = failed_gates[0] if len(failed_gates) == 1 else failed_gates` — A ticket that fails `static` in round 1, passes `static` in round 2, then fails `compile` in round 2 will record `gate: ["compile", "static"]`. The report then counts both `static` and `compile` for that ticket. But `static` did not ultimately block the ticket — it was overcome. The distribution is supposed to show which gates blocked tickets, not which gates ever failed in any round. This is a semantic distortion: a ticket that eventually overcame a gate is still counted as blocked by it.

- [MAJOR] report.py: `for kw, count in gate_counts.most_common():` — The output is now ordered by frequency (via `Counter.most_common`), whereas the old code used a fixed, documented order (`static`, `compile`, `test`, `lock-scope`, `protected`, `expect_green`). Any downstream consumer, test, or human relying on a stable, documented column order will see non-deterministic ordering. This is a backward-compatibility break for the report's output contract.

- [MAJOR] tests/acceptance/test_o3_gate_failure_distribution.py: `assert out.count("test") == 0 or "Gate-failure distribution" not in out.split("test")[0]` — This assertion is tautological and does not verify the defect is fixed. If the word "test" appears anywhere *after* the "Gate-failure distribution" header (e.g. in a gate name, a ticket name, or the "ticket(s)" label), the first clause `out.count("test") == 0` is False, but the second clause `"Gate-failure distribution" not in out.split("test")[0]` can also be False if "test" appears after the header. The `or` makes the whole assertion pass whenever *either* condition holds, so it can pass even when "test" is incorrectly counted. The test would not reliably fail if the old keyword-scanning behavior were reintroduced.

- [MINOR] tests/acceptance/test_o3_gate_failure_distribution.py: The test `test_gate_failure_distribution_counts_each_gate_once` asserts `"compile" not in out` and `"lock-scope" not in out`, but the word "compile" could appear in other sections of the report (e.g. in a finding summary or round detail). The test does not scope its assertions to the "Gate-failure distribution" section, making it fragile and potentially passing for the wrong reason.
<<<END FINDINGS>>>
<<<REQUIRED>>>
- In `loop.py`, filter `failed_gates` to exclude `None` and empty-string values: `failed_gates = sorted({r["stage"] for r in result["rounds"] if not r.get("ok", True) and r.get("stage")})`.
- In `loop.py`, only record gates from the *final* failed round (the round that actually blocked the ticket), not from all rounds: use `r["stage"]` from the last round where `ok` is False, or document and justify why all-rounds aggregation is the intended semantic. If all-rounds is intended, add a test proving a gate that was overcome in a later round is still counted, and update the defect description to match.
- In `loop.py`, audit every `append_ledger` call site (not just the two patched) and ensure each writes a `gate` field for rejected tickets, or document why non-gate rejections are excluded.
- In `report.py`, restore a deterministic, documented sort order for the gate-failure distribution output (e.g. sort by gate name alphabetically, or by a fixed priority list), instead of `Counter.most_common()`.
- In the acceptance test, replace the tautological `assert out.count("test") == 0 or ...` with a precise assertion that parses the "Gate-failure distribution" section and verifies that "test" does not appear as a counted gate. Scope all keyword-absence assertions to that section.
<<<END REQUIRED>>>
